meta.name: Calcium design language
meta.ruleIdPolicy: IDs are explicit, permanent, and never derived from order.
meta.normativeBlockRegistry: Every generic section is an ordered projection of immutable, content-addressed EXAMPLE block records; only explicit current core/atomic records are normative.
meta.ruleIntegrity: Every rule stores a digest of title, text, and section identity. Content changes require a new successor record; supersession changes status and reciprocal links without rewriting the retained content.

(function(){

  "is tracked. The fix is probably a depth counter rather than a flag, but the escaping path "+
  "decides whether that is enough on its own.";
 const THINK="The parser tracks quotes with a boolean, so a nested quote flips it back and the "+
  "run ends early. A depth counter fixes that, but I should check whether escaping is handled first.";
 const RUNS=[{t:"\u25cf ",tone:"default",bold:false,stream:false},
             {t:REPLY,tone:"default",bold:false,stream:true},
             {t:"\n\n\u25be thinking \u00b7 4s \u00b7 312 tok\n  ",tone:"muted",bold:false,stream:false},

 for(const run of RUNS){ const start=at;

   if(ch==="\n"){ box.appendChild(document.createTextNode("\n")); spans.push(null); meta.push(null); continue }

 const rgbOf=s=>{const m=s.match(/\d+/g); return m?m.slice(0,3).map(Number):[212,212,212]};
 const mixArr=(A,B,t)=>"rgb("+A.map((x,i)=>Math.round(x+(B[i]-x)*t)).join(",")+")";
 box.appendChild(gap); box.appendChild(cur);
 const lift=(A,f)=>"rgb("+A.map(x=>Math.min(255,Math.round(x*f))).join(",")+")";
 let head=0,last=0,staticFallback=false; const trail=14;
 const AGENT_MS=9840;
 const clearPaint=sp=>{sp.style.color='';delete sp.dataset.base;delete sp.dataset.s};
 const showStatic=()=>{staticFallback=true;spans.forEach(sp=>{if(sp){sp.style.visibility='';clearPaint(sp)}});
  gap.style.display=cur.style.display='none'};
 const resetAnimated=()=>{staticFallback=false;head=0;spans.forEach((sp,i)=>{if(!sp)return;clearPaint(sp);
  const m=meta[i];sp.style.visibility=(!m.run.stream&&m.start<=head)?'':'hidden'});

  if(staticFallback){last=now;requestAnimationFrame(tick);return}
  if(document.body.dataset.previewMotion==='off'){last=now;requestAnimationFrame(tick);return}

  if(head>total+trail+50) head=0;
  const acc=rgbOf(getComputedStyle(probe).color);
  let lastShown=-1;
  for(let i=0;i<spans.length;i++){
   const sp=spans[i]; if(!sp) continue; const m=meta[i];
   const shown = m.run.stream ? i<=head : m.start<=head;
   if(!shown){ if(sp.style.visibility!=="hidden") sp.style.visibility="hidden"; continue }
   lastShown=i;
   if(sp.style.visibility==="hidden") sp.style.visibility="";
   if(!m.run.stream){ if(sp.style.color) sp.style.color=""; continue }
   const d=Math.min(1,(head-i)/trail);
   if(d>=1){ if(sp.dataset.s!=="1"){ sp.style.color=""; sp.dataset.s="1" } continue }
   if(!sp.dataset.base){ sp.style.color=""; sp.dataset.base=getComputedStyle(sp).color }
   sp.dataset.s="0";
   /* hot edge: overshoot the accent at the head, then cool to the run's own ink */
   const base=rgbOf(sp.dataset.base);
   sp.style.color = d<.35 ? lift(acc, 1+(1-d/.35)*.35) : mixArr(acc, base, (d-.35)/.65);
  }
  /* the cursor sits one space past the head, and goes when the stream ends */
  const done = head >= total;
  gap.style.display = cur.style.display = done ? "none" : "";
  if(!done){ let k=lastShown;
    while(k>=0 && !spans[k]) k--;

      box.insertBefore(gap, spans[k].nextSibling);

})();

rules.title: Registry authority
rules.text: The registry is the only normative source. Generated artifacts filter current records; stable IDs survive reordering and superseded records remain addressable.

rules.title: Three histories
rules.text: Keep one durable event record, one rendered window, and one model context. Eviction changes the window; compaction changes context; neither erases history.

rules.title: Render does not seize ownership
rules.text: A render event may change drawing but never keyboard ownership. Question arrival is an ownership request, not an ordinary render event.

rules.title: Independent carriers
rules.text: Every actionable, status, and interaction distinction has two independent carriers and survives without colour. Dense data may shed colour-only detail only when a named readout preserves the meaning.

rules.title: Orthogonal state axes
rules.text: Lifecycle, outcome, resolution, ownership, focus, pointer, selection, choice, disclosure, availability, freshness, and validity are orthogonal axes; no generic active flag is stored.

rules.title: One ground per cell
rules.text: A cell has one ground. Precedence is owner or armed, copy selection, focus, hover preview, semantic extent, then structural surface; displaced facts retain a mark, edge, or weight.

rules.title: Hover is not focus
rules.text: Hover may preview but never owns input. Focus adds a persistent non-colour carrier so hover cannot be mistaken for focus.

rules.title: Owner routing verdicts
rules.text: Each ownership rung routes an action as handle, reject, pass, or global-intercept; exactly one declared owner or intercept acts.

rules.title: Owner epochs
rules.text: Events carry the owner epoch in which they began and are never replayed against a new owner. An attached child explicitly handles control-C and escape.

rules.title: Pointer commit
rules.text: Pointer press arms a stable id; release on the same id commits. Drag, owner change, identity loss, or release elsewhere cancels activation.

rules.title: Question form and placement
rules.text: Answer form and placement are independent. Choice-only defaults to replace; text defaults to float above the held prompt. A question declares blocking and owner explicitly.

rules.title: Inspection suspends
rules.text: Inspection suspends a question and is not an answer. Every question resolves exactly once as answered, cancelled, or expired.

rules.title: Editor state isolation
rules.text: Editor code is shared; buffers, undo stacks, and histories are isolated by owner.

rules.title: Single approval overflow path
rules.text: Approval inspection is the third choice, labelled show full diff. It has no second key-only overflow route.

rules.title: Motion preference
rules.text: Motion is full, reduced, or off and is independent of colour depth and glyph set.

rules.title: Spinner timing
rules.text: Work spinners use 80–200 ms frames; deliberate wait indicators may be slower. With motion off, a running call keeps a still mark and elapsed text carries liveness.

rules.title: Reduced-motion mapping
rules.text: The HTML preview conservatively maps the operating-system reduced-motion request to off; the product reduced setting may retain essential work or wait motion.

rules.title: Semantic frame contrast
rules.text: Meaningful text remains contrast-safe in every frame; deep fades belong only to a decorative duplicate or mark, never the sole semantic carrier.

rules.title: One-cell animation carriers
rules.text: A specimen animation may change only the glyph in a cell or that cell’s colour, opacity, or brightness. Transform, translate, scale, rotate, and layout motion are forbidden. Per-character stagger is retained. Glyph-swap frames resolve through a one-cell capability rung; ambiguous Unicode falls back to registered one-cell ASCII frames.

rules.title: Meter semantics
rules.text: A meter declares quantity, granularity, and liveness independently.

rules.title: Text coordinate systems
rules.text: Storage offsets, grapheme indexes, token indexes, and display cells are distinct. Editing and public spans never split a grapheme; serialization keeps source offsets.

rules.title: Glyph registry and reserved cells
rules.text: Every semantic glyph declares a collision-free ASCII fallback, width by capability, and reservedCells equal to its widest representation. The renderer pads the selected representation to that reservation.

rules.title: Glyph registry and reserved cells, which bind in fixed columns
rules.text: Every semantic glyph declares a collision-free ASCII fallback, width by capability, and reservedCells equal to its widest representation. Reserved cells BIND where the glyph sits in a fixed column - a gutter, a row lead, a frame edge, anywhere following content aligns to the column - and there the renderer pads the selected representation to the reservation, so changing capability rung moves no column. Where a mark stands in no column, reservedCells records the width of the widest rendering and nothing more, and the mark is drawn at its natural width at each rung. A residue lead is that case: it is followed only by its own count, so it reads as the ellipsis, a space and the count at every rung, and padding it would buy a gap the design does not draw and take the cells from whatever stands beside it.

rules.title: Capability vector
rules.text: Capabilities form a vector, not a ladder. Every action has a base-terminal route; enhanced protocols improve bindings but never create the only route.

rules.title: Linear semantic rendering
rules.text: Every component exposes semantics and announcement policy. Linear semantic events are append-only and non-animated; only the active input editor mutates in place.

rules.title: Terminal control boundary
rules.text: Only the renderer emits terminal controls. User, model, tool, path, URL, and log content is escaped; a PTY interprets controls only inside its emulator boundary.

rules.title: Theme tokens
rules.text: Theme CSS is generated from current token records, including composed ink-on-surface values and preview controls.

rules.title: Resolved action map
rules.text: The keymap, footer hints, and question-mark help are generated from one resolved action and binding registry.

rules.title: Primitive index
rules.text: The primitive index is generated from registered primitives and cites the current rules governing each primitive.

rules.title: Component state tables
rules.text: Every registered component declares entry, carriers, actions, escape, motion-off form, one-bit form, and residue; state tables are generated from those records.

rules.title: Permission posture registry
rules.text: Permission postures and standing grants are explicit, inspectable, and revocable. A grant names the exact command it grants.

rules.title: Call shape
rules.text: A call has one head and one gutter, with at most one bounded body when output exists.

rules.title: Sibling spacing
rules.text: At transcript level, one blank row separates sibling entries; spacing inside a body belongs to that block.

rules.title: Width-bounded nesting
rules.text: Every nested level costs three columns, and nesting is limited by width while the deepest child still clears its own minimum width.

rules.title: Inline-end breathing cell
rules.text: Content stops one column before the inline-end edge.

rules.title: Red semantics
rules.text: Framework status red means failure and override red means unsafe override; red is never the only carrier. Syntax, removal, and identity retain their declared roles.

rules.title: Regional tone budget
rules.text: The tone budget is regional: an entry has three tones, while code, plots, and patches carry their own adjacent palettes.

rules.title: Ground and mark
rules.text: A ground is for an extent; a tone is for a mark. Things take a ground and facts about things take a tone.

rules.title: Ground redundancy
rules.text: An actionable, status, or interaction ground is never the only carrier; dense data owes a readout.

rules.title: Shape-specific focus
rules.text: Focus intensifies by shape: an unpainted run or box inverts, a frame takes its border or axes, a control washes, and a painted identity chip bolds and marks.

rules.title: Semantic motion
rules.text: Motion says that state is changing or something is live. Semantic animation says what is happening, never merely look here.

rules.title: Duration-independent shape
rules.text: A call’s shape does not depend on its duration.

rules.title: Agent bloom ownership
rules.text: The bloom family belongs to the agent and nothing else uses it.

rules.title: Scopes are visible
rules.text: Interaction uses visible scopes, not hidden modes.

rules.title: No typing-scope single keys
rules.text: No single-key command exists in any scope where typing is possible.

rules.title: Scroll is not focus
rules.text: Scrolling is not a scope and never moves focus.

rules.title: Minimum focus reveal
rules.text: Focus pulls the viewport by the minimum displacement required to reveal it.

rules.title: Continuous control commit
rules.text: An inside-bearing continuous control cannot commit its domain value from outside; declared readouts may preview and direct-action controls have no inside state.

rules.title: Pointer parity
rules.text: Every consumed state-changing pointer gesture lands on a state a key can reach.

rules.title: Escape owner path
rules.text: Escape takes the current host owner’s declared safe path at most one rung; in an attached PTY it belongs to the child.

rules.title: No unsolicited reader motion
rules.text: Nothing moves the reader without asking. Rejected commands explain; passive untargeted pointer events may remain silent.

rules.title: Dash is unknown
rules.text: A dash is not a zero.

rules.title: Staleness timestamp
rules.text: A stale reading says when it was taken.

rules.title: Bounded-window residue
rules.text: A bounded window says what it dropped.

rules.title: Refusal reason
rules.text: A refusal states its reason and is never red.

rules.title: Numbers have units
rules.text: A number carries its unit.

rules.title: Copy source
rules.text: Copy takes the source, never the rendering.

rules.title: Histories stay distinct
rules.text: The event record, visible window, and model context never masquerade as one.

rules.title: One-bit survival
rules.text: Every distinction survives to one-bit rendering.

rules.title: Capabilities enhance
rules.text: A capability makes things better, never possible.

rules.title: Set-level width check
rules.text: Width is checked on a simultaneously rendered set, not on an isolated glyph.

rules.title: Pushed-view scope
rules.text: Five scopes included a pushed view and conflated modality with navigation.

rules.title: Geometry-carried ramps
rules.text: Ramp specimens used sub-cell translate, scale, and rotate transforms.

rules.title: Cycle-band spinner timing
rules.text: Every spinner cycle was required to land in an 800–1600 ms band.

rules.title: Generic active state
rules.text: A generic active flag combined lifecycle, ownership, focus, and liveness.

rules.title: Combined live state
rules.text: Live combined lifecycle, freshness, and ownership.

rules.title: Colliding ASCII marks
rules.text: Reader, focus, and current all fell back to greater-than.

rules.title: Attention as failure
rules.text: The attention triangle was labelled and coloured as failure.

rules.title: Second diff overflow route
rules.text: Approval exposed both a third-choice overflow action and a d shortcut.

rules.title: Immediate feedback
rules.text: Every handled input produces immediate visible feedback; a rejected command explains why it was rejected.

rules.title: Reversible action
rules.text: Every state-changing interaction exposes the safe exit, cancellation, or undo route appropriate to its scope.

rules.title: Repeat is scoped and declared
rules.text: A repeating action declares its delay and repeat rate; text entry and destructive actions do not inherit navigation repeat.

rules.title: Ping-pong endpoints occur once
rules.text: A ping-pong alphabet traverses 0 → N → 1 so neither endpoint is emitted twice at the cycle seam.

rules.title: ASCII motion preserves semantics
rules.text: A spinner’s ASCII fallback preserves the shape of its motion, not merely the visual resemblance of one frame.

rules.title: Shared alphabets share timing
rules.text: Spinner sets that reuse a frame alphabet also reuse its interval; a semantic family has one cadence.

rules.title: Watched completion earns notification
rules.text: A watched run that completes while it is not visible emits the declared completion notification without moving the reader.

rules.title: Metric polarity drives trend tone
rules.text: A metric declares whether higher, lower, or neutral movement is desirable before trend colour is assigned.

rules.title: Input windows coalesce by identity
rules.text: High-rate pointer samples coalesce inside their declared window without changing the armed target or replaying against a new owner epoch.

rules.title: Configuration values name provenance
rules.text: A displayed configuration value names the layer or source that supplied it.

rules.title: Unpainted box focus
rules.text: An unpainted box takes whole-shape inversion or lift when focused.

rules.title: Continuous-control focus
rules.text: A continuous control applies its focus wash to label, track, and value as one control.

rules.title: Choice-control focus
rules.text: A checkbox or radio treats its label and mark as one focus shape.

rules.title: Picture focus
rules.text: A picture, plot, or image takes focus on its border or axes rather than painting its data.

rules.title: Focus is not row-shaped
rules.text: Focus geometry follows the component and never assumes one interactive element per row.

rules.title: Focus-first activation
rules.text: Focus-first pointer activation is resolved from state, not from a timing heuristic.

rules.title: Remembered focus re-resolves
rules.text: Remembered focus stores stable identity and re-resolves it when the view returns.

rules.title: Hover may preview
rules.text: Hover may update a declared preview or readout but never becomes focus or commits a value.

rules.title: Legend click toggles a series
rules.text: A legend item is an actionable control whose click toggles the same series state reachable by keyboard.

rules.title: Press arms and release commits
rules.text: Pointer press arms a stable identity; release commits only when that same identity is still armed.

rules.title: Unpaired context click is inert
rules.text: A context-click with no declared keyboard-equivalent action has no state-changing effect.

rules.title: No leader sequences
rules.text: The default terminal profile does not require leader keys or multi-key command sequences.

rules.title: Platform chords remain owned
rules.text: The application does not capture chords reserved by the terminal, operating system, or assistive technology.

rules.title: Bindings do not change availability
rules.text: A binding is not exposed when the same chord works only intermittently under indistinguishable visible state.

rules.title: Table alignment follows value kind
rules.text: Text aligns to inline-start and numeric values align to inline-end.

rules.title: Decimal alignment
rules.text: Comparable decimal numbers align on their decimal separator, not merely their final character.

rules.title: Missing numeric value is unknown
rules.text: A missing numeric value renders as an unknown dash, never as zero or an unlabeled blank.

rules.title: Numeric grouping and units
rules.text: Thousands are grouped and the unit travels with the displayed numeric value.

rules.title: Column-local tail truncation
rules.text: A constrained table truncates from the tail and only in the column that must yield.

rules.title: Sorting belongs to the header
rules.text: Sort state and sort action belong to the column header, which is exposed as a control.

rules.title: Conventional key vocabulary
rules.text: Arrow keys move, enter confirms, escape backs out, tab moves focus, and shift plus an arrow extends selection unless the current owner explicitly captures the action.

rules.title: Bindings remain discoverable
rules.text: The active owner and its primary action, safe exit, and help route remain visible or reachable at every responsive rung.

rules.title: Primitive definitions stay locatable
rules.text: Every primitive record names the canonical sections that define or exercise it; the generated primitive index renders those links beside its definition.

rules.title: Bar alphabets declare placement
rules.text: A bar alphabet declares where it belongs. Determinate work uses a bar only when a total is known; indeterminate work uses a spinner, discrete steps use posts, sub-cell progress uses braille, and ASCII is the universal fallback rung.

rules.title: Ramp meaning precedes appearance
rules.text: Every ramp declares its meaning, semantic use, direction, and attention group. Progress and streaming travel inline-start to inline-end unless an explicitly named exception declares another direction.

rules.title: Help is a durable generated entry
rules.text: Question-mark help emits the generated keymap as a durable, copyable transcript entry with the current scope first and the remaining bindings grouped by scope; docs/KEYS.md is generated from the same binding source.

rules.title: Key choices retain their rationale
rules.text: The keymap records deliberate departures and platform conventions alongside resolved bindings so a later edit cannot recover an incompatible shortcut by accident.

rules.title: Reservations are verified in the composed grid
rules.text: Every registered glyph and delimiter is measured in both Unicode and ASCII forms in the composed browser grid; each form must fit reservedCells and leave the following column at the same coordinate.

rules.title: Normative blocks are registry records
rules.text: Every prescriptive specimen block is owned by a stable current rule record and rendered with its citation. Example blocks remain retained example records; raw section HTML is not a normative source.

rules.title: Subagents · and everything that REPRESENTS THE AGENT takes its hue — the walking mark, t…
rules.text:
and everything that REPRESENTS THE AGENT takes its hue — the walking
  mark, the ramp on its activity text, its own affordance keys. The
  theme accent is main's identity; a child overrides it with its own.

  what does NOT change is everything else: a succeeded call is still
  green, a failure still red, a user message still washed. The hue
  says WHO, and the tones still say WHAT.

  through the parent.

rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:conventional-keys}}
  arrows move. ⏎ confirms. esc backs out. ⇥ moves focus. ⇧+arrow
  selects. ⌃⇧C copies. Every GUI on earth agrees, and a terminal
  app disagreeing with all of them is a terminal app people avoid.

rules.title: Interaction — four principles · {{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:visible-scope}} a mode is something you EN…
Interaction — four principles · {{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:typing-safe-keys}} y to copy, ⌘↓ to the bo…
rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:typing-safe-keys}}
  y to copy, ⌘↓ to the bottom, n and p to move — three traditions,
  none of them shared, all of them invisible. A letter key types a
  letter; in any owner that accepts text it never does something.

  this is the expensive one and it is worth it: it means you can
  type wherever text is accepted, without checking what has focus.

  the prompt is protected by the rule. This resolved profile also keeps
  letters out of the TRANSCRIPT by convention and PROXIMITY: the
  transcript is one esc from the prompt and a reader moves between
  them constantly, so a letter there is a letter they will type by
  accident. A captured block is somewhere you went deliberately.

  so: inside a
  block, 1–9 toggling a plot's series and r resetting a camera are
  legal. In the transcript they are not.

rules.title: Scopes · ⇧⇥ OUT of the prompt, into the transcript — what shift-tab does in every for…
rules.text:
⇧⇥   OUT of the prompt, into the transcript — what shift-tab does
       in every form on the web
  ⇥    forward through the ring, and back to the prompt
  esc  RESOLVE THE INNERMOST TEMPORARY STATE, safely. Its order:
       1  a question is open      take its declared safe path
       2  a substate is open      close find, completion, history search
       3  the prompt has text     clear the line
       4  otherwise              out one rung: block → transcript → prompt
  an attached PTY is capture, not an ordinary substate: esc belongs to the
  child and the displayed host.detach action leaves it.

  “out one scope” was only the fourth case. The one-line version was
  true of the common path and wrong about the other three.

rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:focusShapeRules:continuous-control}}
  learning rate  ├──────●────────┤  3e-4      at rest
   learning rate  ├──────●────────┤  3e-4     focused
   learning rate  ├━━━━━━ ◉ ━━━━━━━┤  3e-4     INSIDE

  the VALUE is INFO and it never changes; FOCUS is the wash; INSIDE is
  weight plus a painted handle. Three states, three mechanisms.

  ★ an inside-bearing continuous control CANNOT COMMIT its domain value from outside.
  Arrowing down a document past three sliders must not move three sliders;
  a declared plot readout may preview without committing; direct-action toggles
  and choices act without an inside state.

rules.title: Key repeat — DAS and ARR · so the app can hold its own timer and the rate is a DECISION — but only when…
rules.text:
so the app can hold its own timer and the rate is a DECISION — but
  only when system repeat is enabled. It never synthesizes repeats for
  a reader who disabled them.

  DAS   delay before auto-shift   170ms   the pause before it runs
  ARR   auto-repeat rate            25ms   40 a second, once running
  and both are per-BINDING, because they are not one question:

  ↑↓ in a list       170 / 25   fast, and it is discrete
  ⌥↑ ⌥↓ page        250 / 90   slower — each one is a whole screen
  a 3D orbit           0 / 16   NO delay, 60fps — it is analogue
  a slider           200 / 40   and it ACCELERATES after a second
  ⌫ in the prompt   300 / 30   slow to start — a mis-hold is expensive

rules.title: The scrollbar · the two directions are not symmetric, and treating them as if they were is t…
rules.text:
the two directions are not symmetric, and treating them as if they
  were is the commonest scrolling bug in a TUI:

  move focus past the edge   the view follows, by the MINIMUM
  scroll away from focus     focus STAYS, and it is still there
                             when you come back

  one row past the edge scrolls ONE ROW, not half a screen — re-
  centring on every step makes the text jump under a reader who is
  trying to follow it.

rules.title: Streaming — the ramp trails the head · The ramp is anchored to the point of arrival, so it advances toward logical …
rules.text: The ramp is anchored to the point of arrival, so it advances toward logical inline-end as text streams—rightward in this English preview. Chrome — the mark and the thinking header — is composed whole and never ramped. The cursor is the AGENT’S OWN MARK, one space past the head — the trail says what just arrived, the bloom says more is coming.Complete streaming preview: Agent says, “I'll look at the current implementation first, then trace where the quote state is tracked. The fix is probably a depth counter rather than a flag, but the escaping path decides whether that is enough on its own.” Thinking, 4 seconds, 312 tokens: “The parser tracks quotes with a boolean, so a nested quote flips it back and the run ends early. A depth counter fixes that, but I should check whether escaping is handled first.”

rules.title: The four spinner rules · {{RULE_ITEM:spinnerRules:one-cell-frames}} by cells() and by the terminal. A…
rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:spinnerRules:one-cell-frames}}
  by cells() and by the terminal. A two-cell frame shifts everything
  after it by one column on that tick — the whole line jitters, not
  the spinner.

  two ways a character fails: it is East Asian AMBIGUOUS (one cell
  or two, by setting), or it has an EMOJI PRESENTATION (one cell or
  two, by font). Registration measures every frame in the resolved
  terminal profile. If any primary frame is not exactly one cell, the
  WHOLE set takes its semantic ASCII fallback — never frame by frame.

  ambiguous-width primary  semantic fallback  interval
  growVertical              . o O @ O o       100ms
  growHorizontal            . o O @ O o       120ms
  noise                     # * .             100ms
  boxBounce2                | / - \\           120ms
  triangle                  v            120ms
  circleHalves              | / - \\           120ms
  pipe                      | / - \\           100ms
  arrow                      v           200ms
  other primary sets use their measured one-cell frames unchanged.

rules.title: The four spinner rules · {{RULE_ITEM:spinnerRules:semantic-frame-rate}} braille 80ms · 10 frames puls…
rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:spinnerRules:semantic-frame-rate}}
    braille      80ms ·  10 frames
    pulse       120ms ·   6 frames
    fullramp    120ms ·  42 frames   ← same rate, more variety
    the walk    120ms ·  82 frames   ← the whole family

  Every WORK set is 80–200ms, from braille at 80 to arrow at 200.
  toggle at 400ms is a WAIT set: its slowness says nobody is busy.
  The semantic class, not one universal band, decides whether it reads alive.
  CYCLE LENGTH decides VARIETY, not liveness: 4-frame sets repeat every
  0.48–0.8s and a 42-frame one does not repeat for five seconds.

  an earlier pass said frames × interval must land in 800–1600ms. That made
  long alphabets look stuck. The band was wrong, not the catalogue:
  frame interval carries liveness; cycle length carries variety.

  the agent's walk is the one exception, and it is deliberate: it is
  not saying a step is in progress, it is saying the agent is alive.
  A ten-second cycle never looks like a loop, which is the point.

rules.title: Six pointer rulings · {{RULE_ITEM:pointerRulings:focus-before-activate}} there is no double-click …
rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:pointerRulings:focus-before-activate}}
  there is no double-click speed. On a FOCUS-FIRST target the first click
  focuses; a click on the ALREADY-FOCUSED element activates it — whether
  that is 200ms later or a minute. Direct-action controls activate on
  their first committed release and have no focus-first precondition.

  so a slow double-click works, a shaky hand works, and there is no
  number to tune. The framework reads no clock for this, which is
  also why it cannot have a timing test even if it wanted one.

rules.title: Six pointer rulings · {{RULE_ITEM:pointerRulings:remembered-focus}} leave a table on row 14, come …
rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:pointerRulings:remembered-focus}}
  leave a table on row 14, come back, and you are on row 14. There
  is no click-to-jump-back in a terminal, so re-entering at row 1
  every time is punishing rather than merely untidy.

  but the element may be GONE — the transcript evicts, a block is
  replaced whole, and the element list is a function of width. So
  it resolves by id and FALLS FORWARD to the nearest survivor,
  which is the scroll anchor's shape reused rather than a second
  mechanism.

rules.title: Six pointer rulings · {{RULE_ITEM:pointerRulings:hover-preview}} ┌────────────────────────────────…
rules.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:pointerRulings:hover-preview}}
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 4.0┤⣀⠡⠤⠒│⠉⠑⠒⠢⡄
  │ 0.0┼──────────┬──────────────────
  │       step 41  ·  loss 0.0372
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  the readout follows the pointer and FOCUS DOES NOT MOVE. It passes
  the every-gesture-has-a-key rule because ←→ set the same store —
  this is the readout half of that pair without the focus half.

  leaving the area LEAVES THE CURSOR WHERE IT WAS. A readout that
  vanished with the pointer would have no keyboard equal.

  and it is consumed only when the INDEX changes — a motion inside
  one sample's columns is a no-op and no frame, which is what makes
  tracking every motion affordable at all.

rules.title: Eight cases that are not edge cases · 1 · ORDINARY CONTENT ARRIVES. Three states, three answers. at the bottom fol…
rules.text:
1 · ORDINARY CONTENT ARRIVES. Three states, three answers.
  at the bottom     follow it. You were reading the end
  scrolled up       DO NOT MOVE. The anchor holds, and the chrome
                    counts what arrived — a button, above the prompt
  navigating        DO NOT MOVE. Focus is a position and a new
                    entry is not a reason to leave it
  an ownership-request event is different: a new question explicitly
  raises its owner and arms it against in-flight input.

  one of these three is wrong in most terminal apps, and it is
  always the second: the view yanks to the bottom while you read.

rules.text:
2 · TYPING WHILE A CHOICE-ONLY QUESTION IS OPEN
  the prompt is held, so a letter has nowhere to land. But a SILENT
  no-op reads as a frozen app.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ⟩ Apply this change?     ▲ answer this first
  › no    yes    {{APPROVAL_INSPECTION_LABEL}}
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
←→ move     ⏎ answer   — esc resolves to NO

  the first keystroke that is not an answer puts that notice on the
  question, once. It is not an error and it does not repeat.

rules.text:
3 · PASTE, IN FOUR PLACES
  the prompt, small    inserted at the caret, as text
  the prompt, large    a chip — [#1 json · 47L] — at the caret
  a text question      into its isolated editor; implementation shared, state separate
  not focused          focus the prompt first, then paste. A paste is
                       a request to type, so it goes where typing goes

  and a paste is NEVER submitted by its own newlines — bracketed
  paste exists precisely so a pasted \n is a newline and not a send.

rules.text:
4 · ⌃C INSIDE A SUBAGENT CANCELS THAT AGENT
  not all of them, and not the parent. You are looking at one, and
  the frame you are looking at is the one your keys act on.

  cancelling the whole fan-out is ⌃C on the PARENT's entry, where
  the head says 3 agents — which is a different place, deliberately.

  ❯ ship it ⚡ now
  ←→ move ONE index and the caret jumps TWO columns. ⌫ removes the
  whole cluster — never half an emoji, never a lone combining mark.

  the same rule the span model takes, one layer down: the unit is
  the cluster and the WIDTH is a separate question.

6 · THE WINDOW LOSES FOCUS
  held keys stop repeating. The cursor stops blinking. Spinners and
  ramps keep going, because the work has not stopped.

  a held arrow that keeps repeating after you alt-tab away is a
  scroll position you did not choose, and the release event never
  arrives to end it.

rules.text:

  a streaming block is replaced whole on every patch, and the
  transcript evicts at its cap. Focus resolves BY ID and falls
  forward to the nearest survivor — the same operation a resize and
  focus memory both use.

  and if the whole ENTRY went, focus lands on its neighbour rather
  than at the prompt. Being moved is survivable; being ejected is
  not.

  wait up to 100ms to appear.

  100ms is the number at which a person stops believing they caused
  the thing. So typing at the window's rate feels like a bad ssh
  connection on a local machine.

  no ⌃x ⌃s, no g g, no space-then-f. A sequence is a MODE you are

  were in it is that the next key did something else.

  remembered.

rules.text:
it is not chrome and not a status line. It is the thing you would
  reach for, so it sits where your hand already is — one row above the
  prompt.

  AT REST it is bgElev, like every other button. It is not active and
  nothing is waiting on it, so it does not wear the accent — that is
  reserved for the thing you are ON.

  and the ⏎ is INSIDE the button, because it is the button's own key
  rather than a hint about the frame. A key printed beside a control is
  a caption; a key printed on it is a label.

  clicking it does the same thing, because every consumed gesture lands on a
  state a key reaches.

rules.text:
↓ 3 new messages ⏎    a reader knows what a message is
   ↓ 214 rows below      nobody has ever wanted this number

  a row is a rendering fact — it changes with the width, with a table's
  columns, with whether a block is expanded. 214 rows is 3 messages at
  one width and 340 at another, and the reader has not missed any more
  of the conversation for being in a narrow terminal.

  and a MESSAGE is what they are counting when they ask what they
  missed — so that is the number the chrome owes them.

rules.text:
I wrote NO SINGLE-LETTER COMMANDS ON CONTENT. But the gesture
  table has 1–9 toggling a plot's series, which is exactly that.

  the rule's REASON was: while an editor owns input, ordinary text keys
  keep typing there without a focus check. The rule bites wherever typing
  is possible; non-typing owners may declare single-key actions.

  corrected: NO SINGLE-KEY COMMANDS IN ANY SCOPE WHERE TYPING IS
  POSSIBLE. Inside a block nothing is typed, so 1–9 on a legend and
  r to reset a camera are legal and good.

  which is the shape of correction this whole exercise keeps
  producing: the rule was right and its statement was too wide.

  a selection cannot straddle two entries

  measured against the catalogue: 8 of 21 sets passed. noise is 300ms,
  triangle 480, bloom 1680, hex 1760. The rule was unshippable.

  the property that actually decides whether a thing reads as alive is
  the INTERVAL: every shipped WORK set is 80–200ms; deliberate WAIT sets may
  be slower. Cycle length decides
  VARIETY instead — 4-frame sets repeat every 0.48–0.8s, while a 42-frame
  one does not repeat for five seconds.

  stated rate was about six times the real one.

  the fix is the exemption's own test: the split is CAUSATION. A held
  arrow is a keypress and the reader is watching for it at 16ms, so
  ORBIT JOINS THE DRAW-NOW SET — alongside echo and focus.

rules.text:
● The parser handles quotes with a single boolean, so a nested
    quote flips it back instead of counting a level.

  ● I won’t add a bypass for the approval gate — that is the one
    path the posture exists to hold.

  ● I’m not sure this is the right fix. I haven’t checked whether
    the tokeniser re-enters this path after an escape.

  an explanation, a refusal and a hedge are the SAME SHAPE, because THE
  SYSTEM CANNOT TELL THEM APART AND MUST NOT PRETEND IT CAN — there is
  no classifier, and colouring an answer by what it seems to mean would
  be a guess wearing the authority of chrome.

  the one thing that DOES change the shape is the content’s own
  STRUCTURE: prose wraps, a fenced block does not. The renderer acts on
  structure it can PARSE, never on meaning it would have to INFER.

rules.title: Where two rules meet — six composition cases · a panel is DISMISSABLE and a question is NOT. Two layers, and one of them is…
rules.text:
a panel is DISMISSABLE and a question is NOT. Two layers, and one of
  them is about to take the keyboard.

  THE PANEL CLOSES FIRST, and its state is held with the prompt’s.
  A panel is a thing you opened; a question is a thing that arrived. The
  arriving one cannot silently sit under something you were reading, and
  stacking two dismissable-versus-not layers makes esc ambiguous.

  and the question still takes the activation guard described in INPUT
  OWNERSHIP — so the ⏎ that would have taken a completion does not answer it.

rules.title: Where two rules meet — six composition cases · three rules want the same moment: a resize keeps your SCOPE (§59), a modal O…
rules.text:
three rules want the same moment: a resize keeps your SCOPE (§59), a
  modal OWNS input (§102), and focus falls forward by id (§103).

  THE LADDER DECIDES, because it always does. The modal owns the
  keyboard, so the resize changes what is DRAWN and not who OWNS it — the
  plot re-solves underneath, the camera is kept, and when the question
  resolves you are back inside the plot exactly where you were.

  ★ a resize is a RENDER event. It can never change the OWNER — which is
  the same reason §59 says it cannot change the scope.

rules.title: Where two rules meet — six composition cases · §97 says an inspection SUSPENDS a question. The queue rule says a second que…
rules.text:
§97 says an inspection SUSPENDS a question. The queue rule says a second
  question WAITS. What does the second one do while the first is
  suspended and therefore not on screen?

  IT WAITS, and the inspection is not a resolution. The queue is of
  UNRESOLVED questions, and suspended is unresolved — which is the
  whole point of the word. Leaving the inspection returns to the first
  question, not to the second.

  EVERY QUESTION RESOLVES EXACTLY ONCE, and a suspension is not one.

rules.text:
the visible window evicts at a cap. A watch retains a stable EVENT ID
  in the durable record, so it can outlive that event's current rendering.

  ⏎ REHYDRATES THE WATCHED EVENT, preserving its identity.
  Completion is a new durable event linked to that watched ID, so it
  appears at the end without pretending to replace history. The watch
  can open either fact; eviction changed only the window.

rules.title: Two selections, and the mouse belongs to the emulator
rules.text: We do not fight the emulator for the mouse, and we do not pretend its selection is ours. Mouse selection belongs to the terminal. Copy takes the source for every copy Calcium performs — direct copy, copy mode, and a copy affordance on a block. A block with a copy affordance shows it on focus, never on hover and never on drag.

rules.title: The render must survive a naive drag
rules.text: A wrapped line's continuation carries no decoration in the gutter; a bounded block's content does not sit inside vertical rules; the scrollbar is the last column, so a drag that stops short of it is clean; nothing meaningful is drawn in a column a reader would not drag through. This is a constraint on layout, not a note.

rules.title: A block is atomic in a selection
rules.text: A block is atomic in a selection: you take all of it or none of it. An extend that reaches a block takes the whole block and continues past it, and the block takes the selection ground on its frame or its first row, never on every cell of its body.

rules.title: A block's copy form, per kind
rules.text: Prose copies as text, unwrapped, with soft wraps removed; code with its original indentation; a patch as unified diff rather than the rendered two-column view; a table as TSV with its header; a plot as its data view; an image as its alt text and its path; a live terminal as its scrollback at the moment of the copy. Copy is in document order, entries separated by a blank line, and a block's content is not re-indented to match its rendered inset — the inset is rendering.

rules.title: esc clears the selection; a second esc leaves the rung
rules.text: esc clears the selection if there is one; a second esc leaves copy mode. A selection is state within a rung rather than a rung of its own, so this does not violate esc popping exactly one rung, and the footer says which press is next.

rules.title: Selection owns the ground, focus keeps its mark
rules.text: Selection owns the ground and focus keeps its mark. At rest there is no ground and no mark; focused takes focusGround and its mark; selected takes selectionGround and no mark; focused and selected takes selectionGround and keeps the focus mark. Selection wins the ground over a diff ground, where the plus and minus marks carry the diff. At 1-bit the selection becomes reverse video while the focus mark persists, so neither fact rests on colour alone.

rules.title: Rectangular copies cells, and says so
rules.text: A rectangular selection copies cells, not source, and says so in the mode label. It is the single exception to copy taking the source, and it is explicit rather than silent. A rectangular selection never crosses a block boundary; it clips to the region it started in.

rules.title: a, A, and no whole-record key
rules.text: a selects the entry under the caret; A selects all loaded entries and says what it did, because the window is not the record; ctrl-A is not bound. There is deliberately no key for selecting the whole record — a key that silently produces a clipboard of megabytes is a trap, and the export path writes a file instead.

rules.title: Three things redraw while frozen
rules.text: Copy mode freezes the frame. Three things still redraw: the mode label in the footer, the selection as it extends, and the count. Nothing else — not the spinners, not the elapsed counts, not arriving content — because a frozen owner that consumes everything is the one rung whose state the reader cannot otherwise see.

rules.title: Buffered arrivals are announced on exit
rules.text: Content arriving while the frame is frozen is buffered and lands when copy mode exits, and the footer says so while it is still frozen.

rules.title: No clipboard is stated, never silent
rules.text: One clipboard with two mechanisms: the operating system's clipboard when Calcium is on the same machine, and OSC 52 when it is not — and OSC 52 is a control sequence, so it is emitted only by the renderer and never from content. If neither is available the mode states it and offers a file instead. A copy that appears to work and does not is the worst outcome available here, because the user will not notice until they paste.

rules.title: A drag scrolls the container the anchor is in
rules.text: The container that scrolls under a drag is the one the anchor is in, not the one under the pointer — the one place the pointer does not decide. The wheel takes the innermost scrollable under the pointer; the arrows take the scrollable you are inside; a drag takes the scrollable the anchor is in, for the whole gesture. A gesture belongs to where it started, which is the anchor binding a gesture to a container the way press-arms binds it to an element. Keyboard extend at an edge scrolls the same container.

rules.title: Three autoscroll bands, and it stops at the container's end
rules.text: Within the rect there is no scroll; up to one cell past is one row per 120ms; one to four cells past is one row per 60ms; more than four past is one row per 30ms. Horizontal autoscroll uses the same bands on columns. Three bands, because two is too coarse to control and a continuous ramp is impossible to stop where you meant. The scroll continues while the button is held and the pointer is outside, even if the pointer stops moving, and stops on release, on esc, or at the container's end — where it stops rather than rubber-banding, there being nothing to rubber-band against in a cell grid. The selection extends to the container's end and does not spill into the parent.

rules.title: A container you pass through is taken whole and does not scroll
rules.text: A container the drag passes through is taken whole and does not scroll, because the anchor is not in it and a block is atomic. Dragging through a bounded block takes all of its rows, not the ones on screen: the window is rendering and the source is the block. A container inside a container is the same answer applied twice — the outermost passed through is taken whole, including its children, and the inner one is never addressable. Where you start decides what you can address; everything you merely cross is taken whole.

rules.title: All-or-none applies continuously
rules.text: All-or-none applies continuously and not only at the end of the gesture: a block joins the selection whole, stays while the drag continues past it, and leaves the selection entirely when the drag returns above it. A block never appears partially at any point during the drag, so the count never shows a size that no release could produce — the count is always the size of what return would copy right now.

rules.title: A high-contrast theme keeps 7 : 1, and says so
rules.text: The two high-contrast themes hold every meaning ink to 7 : 1 against every surface they paint text on, not to the 4.5 : 1 every other theme meets. A theme that promises more than the common floor declares the floor it promises, because a promise no check can read is a label; hcDark and hcLight declare 7 and are held to it at load, on the same path and by the same code as every other floor. Where a ground costs an ink its margin, the theme composes a darker ink for that ground rather than moving the ground — an elevated surface a reader cannot tell from the page is the failure the theme exists to prevent.

rules.title: A high-contrast theme takes focus and selection as bands
rules.text: In a high-contrast theme, focus and selection are bands rather than grounds an ink is composed against: the band declares one colour and one ink, and everything drawn on the band takes that ink, so the theme's ratio holds by construction and no slot can fall through a list. Tone is spent on a banded row, so state moves to the glyph and the outcome word, which is the one-bit rung's carrier asked per cell rather than per terminal; the focus mark persists on the band. Four contrasts bind and the gate checks each as stated: every ink keeps the theme's declared ratio against its own band; the selection band keeps 3 : 1 against the page, because the ground is selection's only carrier; the focus band keeps 3 : 1 against the selection band, because the two can be adjacent; and the focus band keeps only 2 : 1 against the page, because the focus mark already carries focus at the declared ratio and the band need only read as an extent. It follows that the focus band is the one nearer the page and the selection band the one further from it, which is a consequence of the constraints rather than a choice.

rules.title: A floor's scope is every ground the theme paints text on
rules.text: A contrast floor is a claim about a pair, so its scope is every ground a theme paints text on and never a list of grounds somebody wrote down. The focus ground is one of them: a focused region washes its whole extent, bodies included, so a code body's palette lands there exactly as the meaning tones do and is held to the same floors there. Where a ground costs an ink its margin, the theme composes a nearer ink for that ground, keeping the hue and moving only in value by the least that clears; where the palette in question is lent rather than carried here, the composition is authored beside the values it replaces and this document stays normative for what it holds. Three palettes were authored against the page and measured against it alone, and each was found by widening the scope rather than by any failure, which is why the scope is stated as a rule and not left to the list.

rules.title: Availability ranks above a semantic extent
rules.text: Availability takes its place in the one-ground precedence, above a semantic extent and below a hover preview, so that a disabled element keeps its well where an invalid one would otherwise take the error ground. The reason is that tab skips a disabled element, so it is not a thing anyone can act on, and a ground saying that something went wrong on a thing nobody can act on asks for an action the element will refuse. The displaced validity keeps its mark and its outcome word, which is two carriers and neither of them colour, so the rank costs that fact nothing. The state axes are seven and the precedence names three of them, so a composition drawn from choice or disclosure is still unruled; freshness is ruled here only in that it contests no ground at all, because a stale reading dims its content and says when it was taken rather than taking a ground, and the chrome around it does not dim.

glyphs.asciiResolutionNote: The monochrome rung. Above 1-bit the head mark is one glyph and tone carries the state; at ASCII the state carries itself, so this record holds no character — it names the resolution. Pinning `o` here spent the mark `choice-open`/`queued` needs and claimed a fixed ASCII half the rung does not use.

glyphs.asciiNote: `!` and not `^`. The repository has shipped `▲ → !` in two places since C09 §4 — `GLYPH_TABLE.warn` and `GlyphSet.warning` — so `^` split one mark's ASCII half in two, and `^` is already `GlyphSet.cursorMark` (the plot's axis cursor, also `▲`) and `sort-asc`. Nothing but `▲` holds `!` in the row lead.

glyphs.domainNote: Measured over every `›` in the design and not one is a transcript gutter: the agent tape (§095), a question's choice row (§098), a form's button row (§105), the completion menu (§029), history search (§046), the mentions picker (§011), a notification's buttons (§067). `▸` is the row gutter's mark. Recording `row-lead` here spent `*` against the running head mark for a position `›` never occupies.

glyphs.charNote: `─` U+2500, not `—` U+2014. The design draws its rules with the box-drawing horizontal — 82 rules carry it — and the em dash's 448 occurrences are prose punctuation. Both measure 1 cell narrow and 2 wide, so the width class does not move.

delimiters.secondRoleNote: **`»` has a second role and this record is not it.** §003, §004 and §007 lead the mode line with `» auto ✦ …` — a chrome row's lead, domain `row-lead` within its own strip, not a shed count. Nothing renders it yet. Its first renderer registers it as its own mark rather than reusing `tape-right`, whose meaning is *n members are off the right end*.

primitives.name: MARK

primitives.name: CHIP
primitives.definition: A painted label standing for an object; atomic in a wrap.

primitives.name: RULE
primitives.definition: A boundary. Labelled, it announces and never truncates.

primitives.name: WASH
primitives.definition: Focus as a mark plus a ground; the target follows the shape.

primitives.name: LADDER
primitives.definition: Representations of one thing, selected by available width and height.

primitives.name: TAPE
primitives.definition: A window over a list, sliding by the minimum required to hold the current item.

primitives.name: RESIDUE
primitives.definition: A row saying what was not shown and how to reach it.

primitives.name: STATUS
primitives.definition: Banner plus message plus detail, in any container.

primitives.name: BAR
primitives.definition: A meter whose quantity, granularity, and liveness are independent.

primitives.name: SPINNER
primitives.definition: Liveness or deliberate waiting, never progress; declares work or wait.

primitives.name: RAMP
primitives.definition: A static or animated cell-tone transformation; decoration with a declared meaning.

primitives.name: SCROLLBAR
primitives.definition: The thumb is the bar; the track is a divot.

primitives.name: SPAN
primitives.definition: The text substrate; one cell holds one ground.

primitives.name: WIDGET
primitives.definition: The mark says chosen and the wash says focused.

primitives.name: TABLE
primitives.definition: Sheds columns, then stops being a table.

primitives.name: LINK
primitives.definition: Content that acts; active uses a persistent non-colour carrier.

primitives.name: BLOCK
primitives.definition: A bounded body with a frame owned by its container.

primitives.name: CALL
primitives.definition: A unit of work with a result-summary slot; command output is its body.

primitives.name: ENTRY
primitives.definition: One durable event in history; the rendered window is only its view.

primitives.name: QUESTION
primitives.definition: A pending decision with one owner, one safe resolution, and one residue.

primitives.name: OWNER
primitives.definition: The one rung routing keyboard actions at this instant.

primitives.name: INSIDE
primitives.definition: Component rendering of ownership.active when a component has an interior; focus is independent.

primitives.name: SELECTION
primitives.definition: A source range to copy; search hits and diagnostics are separate states.

primitives.name: PANEL
primitives.definition: Floats above the prompt between two rules; dismissable.

primitives.name: PEEK
primitives.definition: Anchored beside an element and takes no keys.

primitives.name: OVERLAY
primitives.definition: Modal and owns input; not dismissable.

primitives.name: PALETTE
primitives.definition: An overlay whose rows are filtered actions.

primitives.name: TOAST
primitives.definition: Transient status, never an owner.

primitives.name: FORM
primitives.definition: A labelled set of editable fields with one submit action.

primitives.name: SPLIT
primitives.definition: Two persistent peer regions with explicit focus transfer.

primitives.name: TREE
primitives.definition: A disclosure hierarchy whose selection and focus remain distinct.

stateTableGroups.title: State tables — seven core facts per component

carriers: ● mark · verb · duration slot · result-summary slot · ⎿ gutter
actions: ⏎ expand / enter · ⌃⇧C copies invocation AND output
motion-off: the spinner is omitted; static ● plus elapsed carry liveness
one-bit: ● still; outcome in bold; the gutter unchanged
residue: ● ok · verb · duration · a NUMBER. Never “succeeded”

extensionRows.label: running
lines: ● white STILL, spinner in the duration slot

entry: a tool, a command or the app needs an answer
carriers: ⟩ mark · focused choice painted · chosen answer keeps ✓ · safe path named
actions: ←→ move focus · ⏎ answer · click a choice · inspect suspends
escape: takes the declared safe path: answer, cancel, or step back one arm
one-bit: › on the focused choice; ✓ remains on a chosen answer
residue: question · terminal resolution · answer when one exists

extensionRows.label: placement
lines: declared; replace is the default · blocking yes · owner question

entry: an answer needs a sentence, not a choice
carriers: ⟩ and the question above the held prompt · shared editor code
actions: ⏎ submits · ⇧⏎ newline · editing operations are shared;
buffer, history and undo are question-scoped
escape: cancels the QUESTION, not the text
motion-off: the caret stops blinking; nothing else changes
residue: question · terminal resolution · sentence when submitted

extensionRows.label: placement
lines: float · blocking yes · owner question editor

entry: a call or a command produced more rows than fit
carriers: the window · a RESIDUE ROW saying how many are hidden
escape: out to the transcript, remembering the row
one-bit: the focused row inverts; the residue row is unchanged
residue: the window and its count. It does not re-expand on its own

carriers: the TRAIL at the head · the agent’s mark one space past it
actions: ⌃C stops the turn and KEEPS the partial text
escape: nothing — it is not a temporary state
motion-off: no trail, no bloom. The elapsed counter carries liveness
one-bit: the trail is a BOLD band; the head band is SGR 7
residue: settled text, no cursor. Nothing replaces the bloom

entry: ⇧⇥ from the prompt, ↑↓, a click, or restored from memory
carriers: the shape’s own treatment · the ▸ mark · the footer’s key row
actions: ↑↓ move · ←→ within a row · ⏎ enter or activate
one-bit: INVERSE, and the ▸ carries the rest
residue: REMEMBERED by id. Inactive focus is the wash, not the paint

entry: a long-running job you started, or /watch
carriers: the footer row · a bar · the entry it points AT
actions: ←→ along the row · ⏎ scrolls to its entry and opens it
escape: nothing — the footer is not a scope
motion-off: the bar stops shimmering; the percentage stays
one-bit: the bar is ## against ..; the name carries identity
residue: it DROPS ITSELF, and the completion earns a notification

entry: a blocked question · a turn over ~30s · a watched run ending
carriers: the bell · OSC 9 · the title — three rungs, all opt-in
actions: none. It is not on screen
residue: the new-messages button, if you were scrolled away

summaryLines: seven required facts per component, all checkable; axis-specific rows may extend them.

carriers: what says what it is — and there are always at least two
actions: what a key or a click does to it
escape: where esc lands, by the published order
motion-off: its form with no animation at all
one-bit: its form with no colour at all
residue: what is left once it settles

lines: prose said all of this. A table makes a missing cell VISIBLE, which is
the failure this document keeps finding — a rule stated in one section
and quietly unstated in the next.
★ two cells that were BLANK until this table existed
a streaming reply’s MOTION OFF form. The trail and the bloom are
both motion, and with both gone nothing said the reply was still
arriving. The elapsed counter had to be promoted to carry it. Every live
thing retains a non-motion liveness carrier; indeterminate or streaming
work uses elapsed time.
a watch’s RESIDUE. It drops itself, so being away meant it vanished
with no trace. That is what put watched-run completion on the
notification ladder.

entry: a call or command returned rows
carriers: a painted header · ▾ on the sorted column · the residue row
actions: ↑↓ rows · ⇥ to a header, ⏎ sorts · ⌃⇧C copies VALUES
escape: out to the transcript, remembering the row
one-bit: the header is inverse; ▾ survives; the focused row inverts
residue: the window, its count, AND its sort — the order is not the
document’s, so the residue says so

carriers: the path rule · a COLOURED stat · −/+ markers · the gutter
actions: ⏎ enters · ⌃⇧C copies a UNIFIED DIFF, not the painted rows
one-bit: the markers alone. Grounds gone, gutter tone gone, text plain
residue: the hunks and the stat. ↺ revert while the turn is recent

entry: a command or a tool produced a series
carriers: the figure · its AXES · a legend · a readout when cursored
actions: ⏎ enters · ←→ crosshair or camera · 1–9 toggle a series · hover
moves the readout and NEVER the focus
escape: out; the camera and the cursor keep their positions
motion-off: a live plot stops repainting on tick; it still patches on data
one-bit: braille survives; the series are told apart by the legend’s
residue: the figure, the final camera, the cursor where you left it

components.title: AN ATTACHED PTY — the CHILD captures ownership over a block

carriers: the border goes heavy · the head says !! attached · the footer
names the child and the reserved host escape
actions: keys go to the child, including ⌃C and esc, except host.detach
escape: goes to the CHILD. ⌃] is the base-terminal host escape;
⌥esc also detaches when the protocol distinguishes it
one-bit: the heavy border is the carrier; the !! survives
residue: the block, scrollable, no longer captured

carriers: a painted name chip · its hue on all four rules · the footer row
actions: ⌃⇥ switches · ⌘1–9 jumps · its prompt is LIVE
escape: its own three scopes. esc never leaves the tab — ⌃⇥ does
motion-off: its walk stops; its elapsed count carries liveness
one-bit: the NAME carries identity; the hue is gone
residue: its transcript stays. The parent records what came back

entry: a paste longer than a few lines, or an @ mention
carriers: the chip · its size BEFORE you attach · a warn past a threshold
actions: ⏎ opens it to edit · ⌥⌫ drops it · it travels with the message
escape: closes the edit view, keeping the chip
residue: part of the sent message, and the transcript shows the chip

summaryLines: six more, and the last two are the ones that had no table anywhere

lines: ★ three more blank cells, and each was a real hole
A TABLE’S RESIDUE had to say its SORT. The rows are not in the
document’s order once you sort them, and a reader who scrolled past
the header has no way to know.
A PLOT’S 1-BIT form could not use colour to separate series, and
nothing said what did. The LEGEND’S MARKS do — which means a plot
with more series than marks is a plot that cannot degrade, and that
is a real limit the plot arm should enforce.
AN ATTACHED PTY’S ESC belongs to the CHILD. It alone sends esc outside
Calcium; other captured owners handle it on the host, while passive rows
may declare no-op or not-applicable. The PTY therefore needs its own
chord and the footer has to say it. Without the table, that cell was
simply never asked.

barPolicy.determinate: A bar is used only when a total is known.
barPolicy.indeterminate: Indeterminate work uses a spinner, never a bar.

rampPolicy.meaning: An animation says what is happening, never merely “look at this”.

keymapPolicy.universal: The universal set gives one purpose to each key and does not depend on what has focus; the active owner resolves that purpose.

platformConventions: ⌥← and ⌥→ remain word-left and word-right in text fields; agent switching uses ⌃⇥ because agents are tabs.

ownedChordRationale: ⌃⇥ and ⌃⇧⇥ switch agents because agents are tabs.
⌘1–9 jumps directly to an agent, matching browser tabs.
⌥↑ and ⌥↓ scroll a page; ⌘↑ and ⌘↓ move to the ends.
⌥p cycles the posture because that setting can surprise; ⌥v reveals per-token values; ⌥⌫ drops the last queued message.

sectionBlocks.renderHtml: {{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:conventional-keys}} arrows move. ⏎ confirms. esc backs out. ⇥ moves focus. ⇧+arrow selects. ⌃⇧C copies. Every GUI on earth agrees, and a terminal app disagreeing with all of them is a terminal app people avoid.
sectionBlocks.text:
{{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:conventional-keys}}
  arrows move. ⏎ confirms. esc backs out. ⇥ moves focus. ⇧+arrow
  selects. ⌃⇧C copies. Every GUI on earth agrees, and a terminal
  app disagreeing with all of them is a terminal app people avoid.

sectionBlocks.renderHtml: {{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:visible-scope}} a mode is something you ENTER and forget you are in. A scope is WHERE FOCUS IS, and focus is drawn. It shows the candidate navigation keyset. OWNERSHIP separately decides which scope may handle an event; being focused does not by itself make a scope the keyboard owner.

{{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:typing-safe-keys}} y to copy, ⌘↓ to the bottom, n and p to move — three traditions, none of them shared, all of them invisible. A letter key types a letter; in any owner that accepts text it never does something. this is the expensive one and it is worth it: it means you can type wherever text is accepted, without checking what has focus. the prompt is protected by the rule. This resolved profile also keeps letters out of the TRANSCRIPT by convention and PROXIMITY: the transcript is one esc from the prompt and a reader moves between them constantly, so a letter there is a letter they will type by accident. A captured block is somewhere you went deliberately. so: inside a block, 1–9 toggling a plot's series and r resetting a camera are legal. In the transcript they are not.

sectionBlocks.renderHtml: {{RULE_ITEM:interactionPrinciples:discoverable-bindings}} at ordinary rungs the footer shows OWNER, primary action, safe exit and HELP. Constrained rungs retain owner plus the highest-ranked reachable safe action; the full resolved set remains reachable through help or its named command. A binding nobody can discover is a binding that does not exist.

Its order: 1 a question is open take its declared safe path 2 a substate is open close find, completion, history search 3 the prompt has text clear the line 4 otherwise out one rung: block → transcript → prompt an attached PTY is capture, not an ordinary substate: esc belongs to the child and the displayed host.detach action leaves it. “out one scope” was only the fourth case. ⇧⇥   OUT of the prompt, into the transcript — what shift-tab does
       in every form on the web
  ⇥    forward through the ring, and back to the prompt
  esc  RESOLVE THE INNERMOST TEMPORARY STATE, safely. Its order:
       1  a question is open      take its declared safe path
       2  a substate is open      close find, completion, history search
       3  the prompt has text     clear the line
       4  otherwise              out one rung: block → transcript → prompt
  an attached PTY is capture, not an ordinary substate: esc belongs to the
  child and the displayed host.detach action leaves it.

  true of the common path and wrong about the other three.

The semantic class, not one universal band, decides whether it reads alive. CYCLE LENGTH decides VARIETY, not liveness: 4-frame sets repeat every 0.48–0.8s and a 42-frame one does not repeat for five seconds. an earlier pass said frames × interval must land in 800–1600ms. That made long alphabets look stuck. The band was wrong, not the catalogue: frame interval carries liveness; cycle length carries variety. the agent's walk is the one exception, and it is deliberate: it is not saying a step is in progress, it is saying the agent is alive. sectionBlocks.renderHtml: {{RULE_ITEM:pointerRulings:focus-before-activate}} there is no double-click speed. On a FOCUS-FIRST target the first click focuses; a click on the ALREADY-FOCUSED element activates it — whether that is 200ms later or a minute. Direct-action controls activate on their first committed release and have no focus-first precondition. so a slow double-click works, a shaky hand works, and there is no number to tune. The framework reads no clock for this, which is also why it cannot have a timing test even if it wanted one.

sectionBlocks.renderHtml: linear mode uses no alternate screen, mouse tracking, cursor-addressed repaint or animation. It never rewrites emitted semantic events; only the active input line edits in place. Choice questions emit a numbered question event and later a resolution event: replace/float is rich placement, never history mutation. Choice questions use numbered choices; text questions use a labelled line editor; mixed forms add an explicit text arm. A running call announces start, useful elapsed milestones, blockage and completion — not spinner frames. Streaming prose arrives in coherent batches.

bindingCatalogues.note: FOUR ORTHOGONAL AXES. Calling a predicate like `focused` a "scope" and putting it in one nesting tree with a region like `prompt` cannot model either. The former catalogues.scopes (prompt/transcript/component) duplicated this with a different third member and drove the displayed count; it is retired.

content-row.note: a transcript or table body row

row-lead.note: the gutter and lead cells of a content row

inline.note: between the fields of a content row

border.note: a frame's own rows and columns — a FIGURE domain. ASCII has no box drawing, so every corner, tee and crossing collapses to `+` and every edge to `-`; a reader tells them apart by where they sit in the frame, not by the character. Uniqueness here would refuse the fallback itself.

plot.note: inside a plot's drawing region — a FIGURE domain, for the same reason as `border`: a mark's meaning comes from its column and row in the figure.

form-row.note: a form or question row — reserved, its first renderer is M16

chooser-row.note: a row of a list you move through — a completion menu, history search, the mentions picker, a question's choice row. Not a transcript row: the design draws the two apart, `▸` for a row's gutter and `›` for the one you are on in a chooser (§017, §018).

tape.note: a windowed strip of peers that slides rather than sheds (§095) — the agent strip is its first consumer. A chrome row, not a content row, so its marks do not meet a transcript row's lead.
